about: Clay's head as fitted architectural pieces (see head_sheets.md): an orange face mass, a dark roof shell fitted over it whose back corners continue as the horns, a nose crest on the front of the roof, a hinged jaw, eyes with lids hinged on the canthal axis, and ear frills tucked under the horns. Model units: z = (700 - px) / 343, y = (830 - py) / 343, from the 1400 px side reference; x = Clay's left.

upper_head.top_note: Between the brow (z 1.706) and where the nose begins (z 1.953) the top line is one smooth bend fitted to the traced points (each moved 0.022 at most): the trace stepped steep, flat, steep there, partly from the side sheet's head being turned a little toward the viewer.
upper_head.note: The orange face mass under the roof. Upper lip line, traced on the side sheet (orange face over cream jaw) and the same in How to Draw and the flight render: from the bottom of the nose it slopes down and back, an overhanging lip that is lowest about a third of the way back (z 1.85); from there it rises in a long, slightly concave line to below the eye, then turns sharply up at the mouth corner (z 1.59) and runs back, gently rising, to the ear opening (z 1.41, y 1.656), where it curls up into the cheek's back edge (anatomy: back edge of the cheek). Traced on the centre of the drawn line. The muzzle hardly narrows toward the front and has near-vertical sides, but it has no flat front wall: its top comes down to meet the front of the upper jaw (the lip), so the roof runs all the way down to the front of the upper jaw, and the nose comes out of the roof's front.

muzzle_taper.note: Bone and muscle, not a box (user: square corners are not believable). The flat top is the nasal bones, the steep sides the upper jaw's bones, and the front the premaxilla: a rounded U in top view (ClayTopShot, the covers). So the muzzle narrows from the eye forward in one long convex curve to 0.86 of its width at the tip, and a small radius (0.03) rounds the front corners. An earlier try narrowed only the last 0.08 to 0.62: a pinched, concave beak under the wider roof plates.

upper_head.ridge_note: The roof is a gable: two mirrored slopes falling from a crisp ridge down its whole length; the ridge is on the measured top profile and the shoulders drop below it (rows: z, drop at the shoulders). The plates are mirrored pairs meeting at the ridge.

front.note: The front muzzle of the upper jaw, in front of the bite point (z 1.86): below the nose its front face is convex (the side sheet's notch at z 1.98 is the nose's underside, not a hollow in the face), then its underside sweeps back and down to the bite point, where it meets the lower jaw's front. That underside is skin, with no teeth. Its bottom corners pull up a little before angling round to the side muzzle. A small brown ridge (the roof's front edge) wraps across the top of the front face right under the nose. From above the front face is rounded across (convex: its middle 0.025 forward of its sides; the roof's front band follows the same curve, so the front ridge runs on from it flush) and bulges forward in side profile (0.01, side sheet front outline), and the front ridge's front edge follows that curve. Its bottom edge, the front lip edge, arcs down in the middle (0.03 lower than at the corners). Simplified: slightly convex, rounding forward (convex_side 0.016); its bottom corners lift only a little (0.012), so they meet the roof's level lower edge.

ridge.note: The roof's front: the front band carries on down over the snout's front face as one smooth piece on the slightly convex front, to a level bottom edge at the overhang's lowest height (eave_y), right across to the front corners, rolling in to the orange muzzle in the same rounded edge the roof has all round (the user's reading). Simplified from an earlier version whose bottom edge rose at the corners and whose rows collapsed and folded (it looked crumpled).

whisker_pads.note: A male lion's muzzle under the nose (user: a lion's nose on a dinosaur's mouth): two fleshy whisker pads swelling forward 0.008 either side of the philtrum's groove, on the orange front below the shield's rim, over the front teeth. Sculpted into the front face (front_setback), so the shield's front skirt above follows them.

front.convex_side_note: The orange front below the shield bulges forward 0.03 at mid-height (was 0.016): with the shield's skirt standing proud above it and the lip rolling out below, a flatter front read as a concave channel (user).

lip_tuck.note: User: the upper mouth looked puffed out, where the references show cheek flesh over the teeth and jaws. Measured on the build: the upper lip's edge stood 0.04-0.055 outside the lower jaw on each side along the whole mouth (wb 0.19-0.235 against the jaw's 0.14-0.18), a shelf overhanging the bite. Anatomy: the upper teeth sit just outside the lower ones and the lip skin lies over them, so the lip edge comes in to 0.012 outside the lower jaw, the cheek above curving in to it (power 2.5: the tuck is concentrated near the lip, the cheek's upper part is unchanged). Faded out at the mouth corner (z 1.58-1.63, the jowl over the jaw muscle) and in front of the bite (z 1.84-1.88, the front muzzle). The upper teeth follow the tucked edge.

upper_head.lip_line_note: User: the jaw curved up at the front like a cereal bowl or a Nike check. The upper lip's edge rose 0.045 over the snout's last 0.1 (1.285 -> 1.33) and the jaw followed it. A reptile's or a dinosaur's lip line is nearly straight: level at the front, rising gently back to the mouth corner. Front rows lowered to 1.268-1.277, which also brings the front of the muzzle further down the face (user: that area had become very small).

lower_jaw.note: A dragon's lower jaw, built from its bones rather than traced (user: the side sheet is a three-quarter view of the snout, so the short chin it seemed to show at z 1.86 was the front of the chin seen at an angle). The dentary carries the teeth forward to a rounded U-shaped chin (the symphysis) at z 1.985, just behind the upper jaw's front under a slight overbite; its tip rounds up and in over the last 0.03 (half-width 0.125 at z 1.86 narrowing to 0.06). Along the tooth row it is about 0.065 deep at the front, deepening steadily backward (0.105 at z 1.75, 0.17 at the mouth corner) as the surangular and angular bones under the jaw muscle (masseter, pterygoid) take over; its underside is one long, gently convex line from under the chin up to the back, where the retroarticular process curves up behind the hinge into the ear opening (z 1.39). Its top edge runs just inside the upper lip line at the front and inside the cheek behind the mouth corner. At the back it is as wide as the cheek (the jowl). Skin: cream with faint pebble scales.
lower_jaw.hinge_note: The jaw joint (quadrate to articular) sits where reptiles have it: at the back end of the mouth line, at the back of the cheek under the back of the eye, level with the mouth line there (which runs back to the ear opening at z 1.41, y 1.656). It was 0.08 lower (y 1.52), and the low pivot swung the chin forward as the jaw opened; level with the mouth line, the jaw drops down and back, its tip well behind the upper jaw's (ClayTopShot, the flying painting).
lower_jaw.squareness_note: a rounded U in section, as the cover shows from below with the mouth open; at 3.6 it was a box, and read as a flat plank when the jaw dropped

bones.note: The lower jaw as bones (jaw_from_bones generates the profile table from these; edit the bones, not a table). z along the head (forward +), y up; model units, before the snout warp.

symphysis.note: The chin's front: where the two dentaries meet, a rounded U just behind the upper jaw's front under a slight overbite. Its last round_len rounds off in side view and from above (tip half-width tip_frac of its width).

chin.note: The chin's lowest point under the front teeth: the dentary's deepest front part.

alveolar.note: The alveolar margin (where the teeth root, the jaw's top edge): bite_gap below the upper lip's edge from the chin back to the mouth corner, so the jaws close together along their whole length.

coronoid_line.note: Behind the mouth corner the jaw's top edge rises inside the cheek (the coronoid process, where the temporalis inserts) back to the hinge region; hidden under the cheek and the jowl's skin.

retroarticular.note: Behind the throat junction the jaw's deep back (angular, retroarticular) lies inside the throat's skin; its underside continues the same smooth rising line up to the ear opening.

bones.depth_note: Deepened from the covers (Dragonet Prophecy, limited edition): the cream lower jaw is heavy, about 0.45 of the upper jaw's height at the front, with a squared chin. Chin bottom 1.213 -> 1.188, symphysis 1.262 -> 1.232.

throat_junction.note: Where the jaw's underside meets the throat (the throat latch). The underside runs one smooth line from the chin, rising more and more steeply into it; there is no notch (user: a drastic stair step from the Adam's apple to the chin).

bones.underside_note: Underside (y): symphysis 1.212 (rounded) -> chin 1.188 at z 1.89 -> throat junction 1.345 at 1.58 -> 1.42 at 1.49 -> up to the ear. Before, the visible jaw ran to 1.285 at the throat while its hidden back followed the cheek line from 1.385, a stair step of 0.1, and its front swept up with the lip line.

lower_jaw.rows_note: 'rows' is no longer read: the table is generated from 'bones' (kept only as the last traced version for reference).

dark_plate_edge.note: The roof's lower edge, traced on the side sheet's colour boundary (dark roof over orange face) and checked against How to Draw and the flight render, which agree on its shape: the roof covers the whole nose, down to the lip at the front; from the nose the edge rises only gently for the front third of the muzzle, then turns sharply up in a near-vertical step at about mid-muzzle, climbs steeply and diagonally to the front of the eye, runs over the top of the eye (the eye tucked right under it), steps up again behind the eye and runs back toward the ear. The rim plates (edge row) follow this line.

eye.note: Round, wide-open eye under the eave; its opening is one teardrop outline: the round eye with its inner corner drawn down and forward into a point, which the pink caruncle fills (side sheet). The lids are two sheets over that outline, and the blink covers the eyeball and the caruncle together.
eye.gaze_note: Out to the side, like a horse's, with only a little forward: the iris sits in the middle of the round of the opening seen from the side (the user's reading). An earlier gaze of 30 degrees forward put the iris toward the front of the opening.

socket.note: The face is carved into a socket that holds the eye assembly: inside the lids' footprint the skin runs in just under the lid dome, and a rounded rim (the orbital rim under the lid-ring muscle) turns it back out to the face.

opening.note: Measured on the side sheet (full-resolution crop, px 98-142, py 232-276), relative to the eyeball's centre in side view, in eyeball radii: the opening (the white's outer edge) is a circle of radius 0.71; the pink point's tip is 1.30 from the centre, 56 degrees below horizontal, forward; its sides close at about 13 degrees either side of the line to the centre. The dark ring round the whole outline: measured at about 0.28 including the sheet's soft shading, but drawn as a thinner line (0.17), which reads right on the model.
opening.ring_note: The liner: a thin line, a little heavier on the upper lid (the painted covers, the side sheet's line). At 0.17 on both lids it read as a broad band, and the lower lid's band stayed behind as a dark crescent when the upper lid closed over the eye (user).
opening.rest_note: At rest the upper lid comes down across the top of the iris (ClayTopShot, Dragonet Prophecy cover: the iris fills most of the opening's height, little white above it), which turns the round stare into a calmer almond; the blink runs on from there.
opening.almond_note: User: the eye doesn't match the references' nice shape. The covers draw an almond: the outer corner comes to a soft point and the upper lid rests over the top of the iris. So the opening's back half tapers from the round toward a cosine point (back_point 0.85), keeping the side sheet's pink inner point, and the upper lid rests 0.26 of the way closed (was 0.17).

snout_turn.note: The side sheet draws the head turned a few degrees toward the viewer: the front of its snout (a darker band from the tip back to a crease at px 80-95) is the muzzle's front face and front corner. Measured as a true side view, that read as extra length and a forward slant. With the muzzle about 0.21 wide, a turn of about 25 degrees accounts for about 0.07 of the sheet's snout, so the snout is compressed toward the eye from z 1.72 by 0.78 (the tip from 2.02 to 1.95), which also stands its front up straighter (the user's reading).

horn.note: The horn grows out of the roof: its root is sculpted into the roof plates, which swell up and wrap its base (a smooth union with fillet radius `fillet`), so the roof's top line runs on into the horn's top line. From there it is a simple S: rising out of the head, flattening as it sweeps back, curling up at the tip (s_curve). Smooth, with hairline incised rings.

s_curve.note: From the side sheet and every official image: the horn comes out of the back of the head rising steeply, flattens as it sweeps back (a smooth downward arc), and curls up toward the tip (an upward arc): a simple S. Root (buried in the roof) at z 1.62, y 1.855; heading 48 degrees above straight back at the root, 7 at mid-length, 62 at the tip; length 0.485, fitted so the tip lands on the sheet's (px 283, py 116). It splays outward from x 0.15 to 0.23. An earlier path through six hand-placed points zigzagged.

ear_frill.note: Measured on the side sheet (frill crop, px 205-262, py 188-224): an almond leaf about 0.18 long and 0.06 wide, from its base at the back of the cheek (front-lower end) back and up to its tip under the horn. It lies close along the side of the head, its face turned outward (the side sheet shows its whole face), cupped like a horse's ear laid back: pale peach hollow inside, an orange rim, the top edge rolled out and over. Its top edge runs back under the horn. Tip re-measured on the gridded crop (px 258, py 190): it had been placed 0.05 too far back and 0.04 too high, so it stood up behind the horn like a spike. Seated outside the neck's shell (whose rim stands at x 0.26-0.27 under the ear's base, probed on the built model), so it shows as a leaf at the back corner of the head, angled a little out toward its tip, as on the Dragonet Prophecy cover.
ear_frill.construction_note: A flap of skin on a thin stalk out of the face's flesh (user: not a solid wedge; a flap that extends from a thin stalk base from the flesh of the face and curls round like a tulip, orange flesh outside and cream inside). Stalk 0.18 of the widest half-width at the root, widest at 0.55 of the length, narrowing to the tip; the section an arc curling 110 degrees at the lower edge and 165 at the upper front edge (the rolled rim the side sheet draws); a thin sheet (0.008) closed round its edges; footprint on the face 0.03 x 0.022, the stalk rising out of it over the first eighth.

roof.note: A thin dark underlay fitted over the face; the visible roof is the plates laid on it (roof_plates). Its eave line is dark_plate_edge.

anatomy.note: Sculpt from the inside out: bone landmarks first, muscle masses over them, then skin creases where muscles meet or skin folds over something that moves. Every entry says what it is and what it does to the surface. Positions are side-view (z, y); offsets act on the side of the face.

bone.name: cheekbone (the line under the eye)
bone.why: Clay's cheekbone is the heavy hooked line under the eye in every reference, measured here from the side sheet: it starts thin below the front of the eye, runs back under it (heaviest beneath the back of the eye), turns up steeply at a corner behind and below the eye, then sweeps back and tapers out. It is the rim of the eye socket: a raised ridge cupping the eye from below and behind, sloping gently up toward the eye and dropping crisply on the outside, where the line is drawn. Sculpted, not drawn.

bone.name: eye socket
bone.why: The bony orbit between brow, cheekbone and postorbital bar. Eye and fat fill it; the surface only seats slightly so the lids stand clear of the face round the opening.

bone.name: back edge of the cheek, curling into the ear
bone.why: Side sheet: the heavy mouth line runs back and up to the ear opening, then does not stop: it curls up and forward round the opening and climbs to the base of the ear frill, so the cheek's back edge becomes the ear. The neck's orange continues behind it, so this is a form edge, not a colour edge: a raised rim, sloping gently into the cheek in front and dropping crisply behind, where the line is drawn.

muscle.name: orbicularis (lid ring)
muscle.why: The ring muscle round the eye that closes it: a soft raised ring framing the lids, inside the cheekbone rim. (No form raises the skin inside eye.clear_radius, where the lids sit.)

muscle.name: masseter
muscle.why: The jaw-closing muscle from the zygomatic arch down to the jaw: the full rounded cheek above the cream jowl, behind the mouth corner.

muscle.name: lip and snout muscle (levator)
muscle.why: Lifts the upper lip; a gentle fullness on the side of the muzzle in front of the eye, below the roof's eave.

muscle.name: temporalis
muscle.why: Fills the skull behind the eye up to the roof; it is why the cranium under the roof is wide behind the brow. Shaped by the face stations, not a brush.

skin.name: masseter fold over the jowl
skin.why: The cheek muscle's lower edge folding over the jowl, parallel to and above the rising mouth line.

skin.name: ear opening
skin.why: The ear opening, where the mouth line ends and turns up into the cheek's back edge.

skin.name: pit at the eave notch in front of the eye
skin.why: A small pit at the corner of the rim's step in front of the eye (side sheet); not the nostril.

expressions.note: Expression comes from muscles. Each muscle action is a shape of the face (a morph target) plus lid bone turns; an expression is a mix of actions, after the Facial Action Coding System (FACS action units noted). Clay's brow is the rigid roof eave, so brow actions move the skin between eave and lid, and the lids, rather than the plate.

cheekRaise.muscles: orbicularis oculi, orbital part, with zygomaticus major pulling the mouth corner up and back

lipRaise.muscles: levator labii superioris (and alaeque nasi): lifts the upper lip off the teeth and wrinkles the snout

lipCornerDown.muscles: depressor anguli oris: pulls the mouth corner down

browLower.muscles: corrugator and procerus: draw the brow skin down and in toward the inner corner; the skin between eave and upper lid bunches over the eye

innerBrowRaise.muscles: frontalis, inner part: lifts the skin above the inner corner of the eye

lipCornerPull.muscles: zygomaticus major: pulls the mouth corner up and back (smile)

lipStretch.muscles: risorius and platysma: stretches the lips back along the jaw ('ee')

lipFunnel.muscles: orbicularis oris: draws the mouth corners forward and pushes the lips out ('oo')

lowerLipDepress.muscles: depressor labii inferioris: pulls the lower lip down off the lower teeth

lipCornerDepressJaw.muscles: depressor anguli oris on the lower lip: the corner's lower side pulled down with lipCornerDown

say_th.tongue_note: positive lifts the tongue's tip toward the palate and front teeth (its three bones turn 0.3, 0.4, 0.5 of it, so 0.3 curls it about 0.36 rad); negative pushes it down through the floor

expressions.pose_columns: lids: turns in radians of [upper lid inner half, upper lid outer half, lower lid]; positive closes
expressions.muscle_actions_note: blink (orbicularis oculi, palpebral part: AU45) is a shape of the lids themselves, built with them
expressions.speech_note: Visemes for speech are mixes of the jaw, the tongue's three bones and the lip actions: AA (jaw open, lower lip down), EE (lips stretched back, lower lip down), OO (lips funnelled forward), TH/L (tongue tip lifted to the front teeth).

roof_plates.note: The plating's layout, now carved into the one-piece muzzle_shield (grooves at these joints, a dome per tile): bands from the front edge back, each a mirrored pair meeting at the ridge, and a rim row of square marginal scutes along the eave. Laid out in profile coordinates: s along the top profile from the front edge back, d the depth below it; joints are lines of constant s.

rows.name: edge row
rows.note: the rim of the roof: square marginal scutes like a turtle shell's edge, thicker than the plates above, their lower edges rolled outward; each one's lower edge steps with the stepped dark_plate_edge

front_plate.note: A plate over the flat front face of the box muzzle, from the top edge down to the eave, above the orange lip band that wraps round the front.

roof_plates.dome_note: After an ankylosaur's skull armour (user: the snout's upper ridge): each plate is an osteoderm, a low dome 0.004 higher in its middle than at its chamfered edges, so the roof reads as bony scutes, not flat tiles.

nose.note: After a great cat's nose (user): the nose leather at the end of the nasal bones, a soft pad coming out of the roof's front and pitched down with it. Section a rounded shield (broad top, sides converging to a soft point at the philtrum), swelling from 0.72 of its size where it emerges to full size 0.04 from the front; the front a low dome (0.018), not a flat face with a rim (the earlier block read as a hollow frame). Comma nostrils at the lower outer corners and a philtrum groove. Side sheet: its top front corner is the nose tip, about (2.02-2.03, 1.443).

nostril.note: Comma-shaped, as on a great cat's nose leather (cover, limited edition: dark slits at the nose's lower outer corners): path is the slit's centreline in coordinates from the front's top-middle (x across, y up, z forward), laid onto the surface; it starts wide on the dome's lower front and curls out, up and back along the side, narrowing to a fine slit.

nose.pitch_note: its axis follows the roof's top at the front, falling 43 degrees toward the tip (side sheet: from (1.95, 1.517) to the tip (2.012, 1.459)), so its top surface is the roof's top surface carried on: it emerges from it smoothly (its back dips under the roof) and juts out at the tip.
nose.size_note: side sheet front outline: the tip juts furthest at y 1.44 (z 2.019); just under it a notch at y 1.414 (z 1.98) where the nose's underside meets the front of the upper jaw, which carries on down to the lip at z 2.0-2.01

philtrum.note: the cat's philtrum: a shallow groove down the middle of the nose leather's lower part, toward the lip

nose.superseded: Not built: the nose is lion_nose, on the muzzle shield.

teeth.lip_note: The upper lip hangs down over the upper teeth: in most images only the lower teeth show, rising plainly from the lower jaw, and the upper teeth show mainly with the mouth open. So the upper teeth grow from the roof of the mouth, inward (inset 0.03) and up (tuck_up 0.02) behind the lip, the front row set back too (the user's reading).
teeth.note: Flight render and limited edition: small, flat, triangular blades. The tooth rows start at the bite point (z 1.86), where the upper and lower fronts of the mouth meet when it is closed: a short row across the front of the mouth there, then rows back along each side lip, each tooth perpendicular to its lip edge, tips raked a little back. In front of the bite point is the front muzzle's underside: skin, no teeth. A little larger mid-row; no single big fang.

upper.inset_note: From the tucked lip edge: the upper teeth stand just outside the lower ones (lower inset 0.016 from the jaw edge).
upper.outside_note: The upper tooth row sits 0.01 outside the lower one (whose row is 0.016 inside the jaw's edge), never outside the lip. Placed from the lip alone, the back upper tooth stood outside the lower jaw at the mouth corner and hung down past it as a blade.

teeth.shape_note: Re-read on the two open-mouth paintings (Dragonet Prophecy cover, ClayTopShot): cones, not flat blades, about 1.4x the earlier length for the upper teeth (hidden behind the lip when shut), 1.15x for the lower (which show along the closed lip); round-based (thickness about the base's width), still tips raked back, still no single big fang. Sculpted as a reptile's teeth (user: not flat triangle shards): each a cone rooted 0.004 into the gum, its section an oval flattened side to side (along the jaw 0.45 of its length across the base, 0.012 thick), tapering to a sharp tip that curves back toward the throat by 0.18 of its length (front row 0.09, flattened front to back).
teeth.size_note: Stout cones as the covers paint them: across the base 0.6 of the tooth's length along the jaw, 0.018 thick.
teeth.row_note: The rows run the whole jaw, to the front of the mouth (they stopped at a bite point at z 1.86 while the jaw was traced short from the side sheet).
teeth.count_note: Re-read on the Dragonet Prophecy cover's open mouth: about six or seven stout cones show along each side of each jaw, with gaps between them, not a saw of small spikes. Upper 7 per side (0.042-0.064 long), lower 6 (0.03-0.046).

mouth.why: The mouth opens by stretching skin, not as two rigid pieces parting (user; Dragonet Prophecy cover). The cover's open mouth is a deep cavity, its floor a trough for the tongue under an arched palate, and the gape ends in a rounded corner of cheek skin under the eye. The lips stay joined from the corner back to the hinge, where the jaw's bone runs on inside the cheek.
mouth.corner_note: The web's front edge is closed by a half round from the skin into the lining, and the web thickens toward it (0.004 + 0.008 u^3), so the mouth's corner is a fleshy commissure. Before, the two loose sheets 0.004 apart showed as a thin pale sliver at the corner of the open mouth.
mouth.cheek_bulge_note: the outward bow of the cheek skin at the jaw's full opening (jaw 0.6 rad), as a corrective shape the jaw drives (jawOpen = jaw / 0.6)

lip_roll.note: The lips' fleshy margins (user: lips convincing for expression and speech): a rounded rim 0.004 proud along each lip, centred 0.006 from its edge, on the upper lip (face) and the lower (jaw), so the mouth has soft lips that the muscle actions move, not cut edges.

tongue.note: A muscular tongue (user: convincing for speech): rounded across, a shallow median groove (0.004) down its middle, thick at the root (0.03) thinning to 0.012, its tip broad and rounded over the last 0.14 of its length, lifting a little off the floor, lying in the floor's trough. On three bones (tongue1-3) so it can curl up for speech sounds.

muzzle_shield.note: The muzzle shield (user): one solid piece over the top of the head, from the snout's front back to the roof's end, wrapping down over the front of the snout, its edge rounded all round. Its plating is carved into it, like an ankylosaur's fused skull armour: grooves at the band joints, down the ridge and along the rim row (layout from roof_plates.layout), and a low dome in each tile. It replaced separate tiles plus a front cap fitted to the front curve, which read as a workaround. The lion's nose rises out of it (lion_nose).

groove.note: a V-ish groove at each joint: depth 0.005 of the 0.009 shell, fading out over 0.0035

ear_clearance.note: Designed in (user: the part near the ears kept reaching out and clipping them): the ear's top edge per station, measured from the built ear mesh (FrillL, max y per 0.02 of z), plus a margin. Behind the eye the shield's lower edge runs above it (a smooth max with the traced edge), so the shield never meets the ear's path. Re-measure if the ear moves.

muzzle_shield.skirt_note: The front skirt's thickness rounds off toward its side ends and its bottom edge (edge_round), like the rest of the shield's edge; at full thickness to its ends it stood out as square tabs at the bottom corners.

lion_nose.note: A male lion's nose on the front of the muzzle shield (user, walkthrough): a short bridge (s 0.13 to the cap, about 0.06 long) rising out of the shield's top just behind its front, flat-topped with crisp corners to upright sides (squareness 7), ending in the leather cap, whose front is its own flat face (the nose leather, 0.72 of the cap's section) with a small bevel (0.008) round its edge, set just behind the shield's front edge (s_front 0.012) so the shield's rim carries on round the front ahead of it. Before: the bridge ran from mid-muzzle (s 0.30), too long, too high on the shield, its section soft and its front a dome. Same material as the shield. s is distance along the top profile from the shield's front edge (before the snout warp).
lion_nose.stations_note: s, half-width, height above the shield's surface: the cap (s 0.03-0.11) broad and full, a slight waist where it meets the bridge, the bridge narrowing and settling into the shield toward its root.

nostril.note: Comma nostrils on the cap's flat face: path points are (x across, fraction of the cap's height), from the wide inner end low on the face curling out and up; cut back into the nose along its axis.

lion_nose.fillet_note: The bridge's sides flare out at its base by up to 0.014, so it grows out of the shield instead of sitting on it as a rod.
lion_nose.face_note: The cap's face is an upright plane facing forward through the cap's top front corner (s_front 0.025), its edge rounded over 0.01: cut perpendicular to the steep front slope instead, it faced down and showed from the front only as a thin band with the nostrils crowded into it.
